primitives.breakdown_regime: When A_{obj} > T, object O becomes functionally invisible or inaudible.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that hypnotic phenomena arise from incomplete cognitive monoideism—whereby consciousness partitions into dominant and subordinate subsystems. This leads to a dualistic mode where background thoughts persist but cannot inhibit motor or associative responses. The primitive 'monoideism_incompleteness' formalizes this as a partial order on mental states. 'Background thought inhibition' captures how these residual thoughts can comment but not constrain action, forming a kernel of non-inhibitory cognition. 'Selective anesthesia' extends this to sensory modalities, showing that suggestion can locally suppress perception based on object identity. These primitives form a triadic structure: cognitive partitioning → commentary without control → localized sensory suppression. Each operates within a breakdown regime where increasing incompleteness or suggestion strength causes failure of normal inhibitory mechanisms. The epistemic trace reveals a dual nature of consciousness: both structured and fragmented, capable of self-monitoring yet susceptible to override.
